documented semantics (replaces the withdrawn 'not found' guard mutation): when the order vanishes between the duplicate check and the read, the core's SELECT INTO leaves an all-NULL record, so the owner check fails closed to 'forbidden' - never a raised error, never an admission (the suspected 'unassigned record' exception does NOT occur)

static: every APPLY/ROLLBACK pack = ONE BEGIN, SET LOCAL lock_timeout 5s then advisory lock 2979301232487107403 then SET LOCAL lock_timeout 5s as the exact statements 2-4 after it (tightened from: lock is statement 2), one COMMIT last, drift guard, no data DML, no secrets
generator is reproducible: build.mjs --check is clean (packs == inputs)
replica sanity: the installed ORIGINAL functions equal the captured prod text (pg_get_functiondef == facts) and DRIFT_QUERY/POSTCHECKS(S0) read S0_original
APPLY-01 on the original: succeeds, retained SELECT all ok, state S1, POSTCHECKS(S1) ok; check_in_ticket still original
APPLY-02 after 01: succeeds, state S2, POSTCHECKS(S2) ok
apply order is enforced: APPLY-02 on the original (core absent) refuses with DRIFT and changes nothing
second run refuses cleanly: APPLY-01 twice and APPLY-02 twice (DRIFT, nothing changed)

UNSAFE (explicit-override) ROLLBACK restores the captured originals EXACTLY: byte-identical pg_get_functiondef and prosrc, equal sorted ACL, config, owner; core gone; schema private and its four incident tables KEPT and identical; data untouched
rollback order is enforced and the (override) rollback has its own drift guard
advisory lock serialises two runs: B waits on the advisory lock while A holds the transaction open, then B refuses cleanly (DRIFT); end state S1
lock is shared across packs: a concurrent ROLLBACK/APPLY of a different pack also queues (same key)

TIMEOUT (lock_timeout follow-up): A (real APPLY-01) holds the pack lock ~7 s; B (the same pack) waits on the advisory lock and fails with SQLSTATE 55P03 lock_not_available after ~5 s (4.5-6.5 s), not after A's ~7 s; A is unaffected (commits, state S1); B changed nothing and holds no advisory lock afterwards

NEGATIVE CONTROL for P14: the same APPLY-01 with the PRE-lock lock_timeout removed (timeout only after the lock, the literal 'after the lock' placement) is NOT bounded: B waits out A's whole ~7 s hold and then refuses with DRIFT (not 55P03)
PRECHECK-12A.sql runs read-only (READ ONLY transaction), errors on nothing, and leaks no row contents (sentinel email/handle/tokens absent from output)

12A changes NO table, column, policy, grant, index, constraint, trigger, RLS flag, other public function or table data (catalog+data fingerprint equal before and after both packs); every other reader of event_orders/status/checked_in_at is therefore untouched
NEGATIVE CONTROL for R01: an added index, a changed policy, a changed grant, or a changed other function each make the fingerprint differ (the fingerprint can fail)

WRITE-SET EQUALITY: after the same raw-token scan sequence the whole event_orders table is identical on the original and the hardened functions except nothing (admission still writes ONLY checked_in_at; status is never rewritten) - for both RPCs
NEGATIVE CONTROL for R02: a hardened core that ALSO rewrote status to 'checked_in' makes the table differ from the original (the comparison can fail)

LIVE CROSS-CHECK vs adapter: every result code the real hardened functions return (scan: admitted, already_used, unpaid, forbidden, invalid, empty, unauth; ticket: same minus empty, which check_in_ticket folds into notfound->invalid) maps to the SAME canonical code through adaptScanResponse / adaptTicketResponse, never to 'error'; keys outside the adapter whitelist are only message/order_status; an unmapped code maps to 'error' (negative control)

VERIFY-12A.sql runs read-only, returns only counts/catalog facts (no fixture contents), reports zero TEST ATLAS rows on the replica, and COUNTS a planted 'TEST ATLAS' event/order/user (negative control)

optional UNIQUE-index pack, static: APPLY/ROLLBACK have NO BEGIN/COMMIT/advisory-xact-lock, exactly one CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (partial, WHERE qr_token IS NOT NULL, no IF NOT EXISTS) / one DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS; PRECHECK and POSTCHECK are SELECT-only; no data DML; no secrets
optional pack PRECHECK on the replica: read-only, aggregates only, reports the duplicate (surplus 1, gate proceed=false) and, after the duplicate is removed, proceed=true; no token/contact leaks
optional pack, NEGATIVE CONTROL: with a duplicate token present the CONCURRENTLY build FAILS (23505) and leaves an INVALID index; POSTCHECK reports not ok; ROLLBACK removes it

optional pack on a duplicate-free replica: APPLY succeeds, POSTCHECK every row ok (valid, unique, partial, qr_token), a duplicate token is refused 23505, NULL tokens still insert, and the hardened door still admits / refuses exactly as before
optional pack, NEGATIVE CONTROL for 'must be non-transactional': the same CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside BEGIN..COMMIT is refused (25001) and creates nothing
optional pack ROLLBACK: drops the index (idempotent, second run is a no-op), data untouched, door unaffected; the index is invisible to 12A's own drift guard (state still S2 after APPLY)
